the magnitude of the errors in subjective assessments of the likelihood and severity of ecological risks can be reduced by a factor of 3 to 4, and that the errors in the estimates of the costs and risks of stochastic processes can be reduced to 10% to 20% of their original values.

(1) ecological risk assessments involve many sources of uncertainty that are not acknowledged in current approaches; (2) subjective assessments of the likelihood of ecological damage are highly uncertain; (3) subjective assessments of ecological risk are highly uncertain; and (4) the uncertainties associated with subjective assessments of ecological risks can be reduced by considering a few kinds of uncertainties.
(i) subjective assessments of ecological risk are subject to large errors, and (ii) these errors can be reduced substantially by consideration of a broad range of sources of uncertainty.
